title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to crayon website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the crayon website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

## Screenshots

description:
Fixes #104, sort of

I realize you will probably want to implement your own fix, but this *almost* fixes things for me. I thought it was worth getting the ball rolling in any case.

However, since I attach devtools in `.Rprofile`, when crayon is first loaded, RStudio's color capabilities still aren't being detected correctly. But if I comment that out, this fix works. Or if I manually call `crayon:::rstudio$detect(clear_cache = TRUE)` in a session, things are fixed. I believe that has something to do with rstudioapi and the startup process? But that's a real problem, because devtools will often appear in `.Rprofile` (at least for some of us).

title: Enable colors on GitHub Actions

This will work, but I am not sure it is much better than the existing solution of setting the option in setup-r.

I tried a few different ways of not doing this and using a fake tty using script / unbuffer (https://github.com/jimhester/r-actions-test/runs/932366132?check_suite_focus=true#step:10:21) but that doesn't handle `\r` like we would want, so the log while colored looks bad.

Maybe instead of doing this PR we should just set the crayon option just in the workflow step for rcmdcheck?

Avoid warning if INSIDE_EMACS does not contain version.
description:
The INSIDE_EMACS environment variable is not guaranteed to include the version
number. For example, https://github.com/akermu/emacs-libvterm sets it to
"vterm". To avoid warnings in this case we remove all non-numeric characters and
return NA if nothing remains.

title: Allow multiple ANSI tags per style code
description:
Changed `codes` to contain lists so that we can use multiple tags per code, although in practice we only use this for `reset` built-in style.  While this is added complexity, it only affects the package onload, and even then performance cost will be minimal.  This allows:

![screen shot 2016-08-23 at 8 24 17 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/6105908/17914384/a031fafe-696f-11e6-87ee-9a8e17e748d7.png)

Main drawback is that we that we add a bunch of extra close tags that consume bytes, but that seems like a minor side effect.  As a result this did require updating two existing tests although the displayed output is unchanged for them if you `cat` the results.

Ended up being easier to implement fully than to mock up, so here it is.

title: adding crayon strwrap analog to base strwrap function
description:
I really love using crayon, but using base `strwrap` with crayon strings often cuts lines short due to the length of the extra formatting characters. 

I wrote up a small function that strips the style of the crayon text, uses base `strwrap` on the stripped text, then uses `col_substr` to build each line to the correct length. I also added a pretty extensive test that loops over a bunch of permutations of various input parameters and compares the stripped `col_strwrap` output against the base `strwrap` output of stripped text.  

Hopefully this is useful for the package!

title: fix inside_emacs()
description:
Since I upgraded to Ubuntu 17.04 with Emacs 25.1.1 (with ess from elpa 20170501.306), I noticed that crayon stopped coloring.

It seems that there the environment variable `EMACS` is not set:

```r
> Sys.getenv("EMACS")
[1] ""
```

Using the `INSIDE_EMACS` instead brings the coloring back.

Probably could come up with further optimizations, but these are minimally intrusive and produce enough improvements that they seemed worth the trouble.

title: Remove Dependency to `memoise` and `digest`
description:
### TL;DR
- found funny bug involving `memoise` and the `crayon` CRAN _binary_ package
- realized you can remove dependency to `memoise` and `digest` with almost no additional code by using a closure
- created this pull request that removes that dependency

@jimhester, I'm guessing this issue is of interest to you given the link to `memoise`.  Also, I apologize for lobbying for the removal of `memoise` as an import for `crayon` and hope you find my request is not completely crazy even if you don't agree with it.
### Whole Story

I ran into a rather bizarre bug involving `memoise` that made it impossible to `forget` the cached version of `crayon:::i_num_colors`.  Somehow, the binary version of `crayon` on CRAN has a corrupted copy of the memoised `crayon:::i_num_colors` function:

```
ls(all=T)
# character(0)
install.packages("crayon")
# trying URL 'http://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/mavericks/contrib/3.2/crayon_1.3.1.tgz'
# Content type 'application/x-gzip' length 604079 bytes (589 KB)
# ... snip
str(crayon:::i_num_colors)
# function (...)  
#  - attr(*, "memoised")= logi TRUE
```

Notice how the function does not have a memoise class as it should ([full session transcript on gist](https://gist.github.com/brodieG/6101ada64d917b4b659d)).  This causes `is.memoised` to fail, which then prevents `forget` from working.

Installing from source everything works fine:

```
remove.packages("crayon")
q()  # and restart R
install.packages("crayon", type="source")
str(crayon:::i_num_colors)
# function ()  
#  - attr(*, "memoised")= logi TRUE
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "memoised" "function"
```

I also rebuilt the package binary and installed it, and everything was fine, so something funny happened with the CRAN binary build process.

All that aside, while debugging this problem I realized that the `memoise` and `digest` dependencies of your package hinge only on memoising `crayon:::i_num_colors`.  Since that function doesn't even take arguments I think it makes sense to use a closure to handle the memoization rather than add dependencies to a lot of functionality that is not really needed (granted, as far as adding dependencies `memoise` and `digest` are probably as good as it gets).

I think your package is awesome and should be used by anyone writing packages producing meaningful amounts of text output.  I initially balked at the idea of importing your package into mine due to my desire to keep my package download small and as such minimize the dependency footprint, and that all I needed was to color some stuff red or green.  In fact, I went so far as to borrow a subset of the `crayon` functionality and put it into another package without dependencies until I realized how silly that was (which btw was around the time I realized I needed to `substr` colored strings and discovered you'd already handled all the painful stuff you need to do with closing and re-opening escape sequences).

I'm going to import your package no matter what, but hopefully you'll consider removing the dependencies to `memoise` / `digest` to make this package stand alone, especially since the change required to do so is so minor.
### Other Notes

I added some tests, and in the process of re-running tests and checking the package I ran into a couple of issues:
- I had to change how options were being re-set in `test-has-colors.R`
- I had to remove references to `%:%`; I have no idea where to find that function and it doesn't seem to be part of this package or any of the dependencies I removed, and google is totally useless it telling me where it comes from.  I inferred that it is a safe version of `:` (i.e. won't fail with `1:x` where `x==0`) and replaced it accordingly
- I had to add `:::` references to non-exported variables in `test-make-style`

title: Get crayon to load in R session launched via emacs tramp
description:
The Emacs tramp package wraps the INSIDE_EMACS variable in single quotes, as seen [here.](http://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/tramp.git/tree/lisp/tramp-sh.el?id=f4c5c4ba8990f7d7c2243db86144969b0d4c004e#n475)

These quotes leads to the following error when loading crayon

```
> library(crayon)
 Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'crayon', details:
   call: if (inside_emacs() && emacs_version()[1] >= 23) {
   error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
 In addition: Warning message:
 In emacs_version() : NAs introduced by coercion
 Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘crayon’
```


This error also prevents the loading of packages that import crayon such as testthat. Seems safe to remove the single quotes, which eliminates all these errors.

title: Fix for tput with uninformative output
description:
The tput installed on winbuilder gives an 'unknown terminal "cygwin"'
error on STDERR, but returns nothing on STDOUT and returns an error code
of 0.  Therefore the result cannot be coerced to a number and
cols returns character(0).

`character(0) %in% c(0, 1)` returns `logical(0)`, and `logical(0)` in an if
statement yields the fairly useless error message 'error: argument is of
length zero'

This situation results in crayon being unable to load.  The fix handles
the above situation as well as the situation where tput does return
something on STDOUT, but that value cannot be coerced to a number (and
returns NA).

Fixes #18
